newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian share prices hit six-month low.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian share prices hit six-month low.

text.p: Egyptian share prices hit a six-month low on Sunday in sluggish trading which saw a handful of deals in the milling and cement firms.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index, which closed lower all last week, shed 3.29 points to 341.03 points -- its lowest level since January 20 when the index closed at 337.04 points.
Almost half the 87 traded shares closed lower, while 16 stocks rose and 28 ended unchanged, the CMA said. Turnover was a below average 39.87 million pounds ($11.75 million).
The market was closed on Thursday for a public holiday.
"No one knows what is going on or why this is happening," said broker Yasser Darwish at El Rashad Securities Brokerage.

"People appear to be pessimistic, but I can't see any fundamental reason why the market is falling. All I can say is that prices are cheap and investors must take advantage of that. Everything is on sale," he added.
Some traders said individual investors had either given up on the market or were on their summer holidays.

Darwish said institutions and foreign investors were the main buyers, focussing on the cement and milling sectors because of good results and low price-to-earning ratios, but added that prices were barely affected because of plentiful supply.
"They (foreigners and institutions) come in and want to buy in bulk and they find it easily, without any pressure on prices," he added.

Egyptian Portland Tora Cement, the day's most active share with more than six million pounds traded, rose one pound to 86. Suez Cement, which is expected to give out a 4.5 pound dividend soon, lost 1.99 to 66 in relatively busy trading worth 2.3 million pounds.
Investors also scooped up Helwan Portland Cement and Amriya Cement shares but prices were mixed. Helwan fell 1.1 pounds to 66.75 while Amriya gained 1.15 to 81.15.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills was the star of the milling sector with turnover worth 2.4 million pounds, but the stock ended unchanged at 71.5 pounds.
Eastern Tobacco, the country's monopoly cigarette maker, also put in a strong showing, trading in shares worth more than three million pounds. But the stock lost 0.2 to 89.99.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 462.65 points from 471.31 points on Wednesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms also slipped to 253.4 points from 254.71
